title: Edge times from 2009 to 2025 show that the ZTF-CBO-4 occultation becomes 0.47 d shorter each year, and that the published periods of six disk-occultation candidates have errors that are too small
abstract: Question: Do the ephemerides of the six ZTF circumbinary-disk occultation candidates of Hu et al. 2026 (arXiv:2601.16828) predict later and earlier data, and do the occultation edges move in time, as disk precession predicts? Method: We measured the half-flux ingress and egress time of each cycle in ZTF DR24 (2018-2025; data after October 2024 are a hold-out), fitted linear O-C trends with a cycle-jitter term, measured edge offsets in Pan-STARRS1 detections of 2009-2014, tested Harvard DASCH plates (1934-1986) and NEOWISE (2014-2024) for the brightest candidate, ZTF-CBO-1. Results: The occultation of ZTF-CBO-4 (P = 30.26 d) becomes shorter by 0.0385 +- 0.0072 d per cycle (0.47 +- 0.09 d per year, 5.3 sigma): the egress comes earlier and the ingress later; the 2012 PS1 egress agrees with the ZTF-only trend (+1.95 against +1.87 +- 0.91 d), and all four 2025 egresses are 1.3-1.4 d earlier than the published ephemeris. Edges scatter by up to 3.4 d from cycle to cycle, so the published period errors are too small (for example ZTF-CBO-1: 529.32 +- 0.03 d published; 528.7 +- 0.3 d from PS1 and ZTF edges). PS1 edge times agree with linear extrapolations of the ZTF edges for all six objects (-0.8 to +2.6 sigma). No DASCH plate at a predicted occultation phase detects ZTF-CBO-1 (0 of 7, against 12 of 17 at other phases; Fisher p = 0.002), but random phase shifts give this result 11-18 percent of the time, so the plates agree with century-long occultations without fixing the phase. During occultation ZTF-CBO-1 keeps 30-35 percent of its optical light but 42 percent (W1) and 46 percent (W2) of its infrared light: an unocculted source of about 1160 K (930-1580 K) gives 7 percent of W1 and 14 percent of W2; a blend or a stellar companion does not explain it, hot dust does. Limitations: few cycles for long periods; jitter of some edges is poorly known; ZTF-CBO-5 and -6 are blended in ZTF; ramps are linear; the infrared result assumes blackbody stars; no spectra or radial velocities. display.caption: Ingress (blue) and egress (orange) mid-times of the six candidates relative to the published ephemerides. Filled circles: ZTF to October 2024; open circles: ZTF hold-out to October 2025; squares: Pan-STARRS1 2009-2014; lines: linear fits with cycle jitter. ZTF error bars are formal only. In ZTF-CBO-4 the egress drifts earlier and the ingress later, so the occultation becomes shorter.

ZTF-CBO-1: fraction of light that remains during occultation against wavelength. The grey line is a two-star model fitted to the optical points. NEOWISE W1 and W2 are above the model, which shows an unocculted source of about 1160 K.
